claim: A publisher that fails its first MQTT broker connection during the boot window (because HA/broker is still starting) and then never retries sits dead indefinitely — its entities stay Unknown/Unavailable until manually restarted.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must retry broker connection with backoff (rumqttc poll loop) and/or systemd ordering (After=mosquitto) to survive NixOS boot races
scope_conditions: CumulusMX on RaspiOS host, HA OS in Proxmox VM on Raspberry Pi 5, Feb 2025
quoted_support: The problem seems to be a delay between CumulusMX and Home Assistant booting up. CumulusMX is up a few seconds after system reboot, while HA takes a few minutes ... It looks like that causes CumulusMX to fail to connect to the broker and then simply not trying again it seems.

claim: Changing the retain flag on a publisher's discovery/config messages caused HA to rediscover entities under their original names, breaking dashboards — retained-message churn has UI-level blast radius.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should treat retain semantics of its discovery messages as stable config; flipping retain in an upgrade path is a breaking change needing entity-name migration
scope_conditions: CumulusMX MQTT config, retained vs non-retained topics
quoted_support: I changed the MQTT configuration in CumulusMX to not retain, deleted the retained topics and rebooted. The sensors are back, but returned to their original names, breaking the dashboard again.

claim: MQTT auth setup choice (creating a 'homeassistant' MQTT login vs an HA mqtt user) interacted with entity re-discovery: deleting and reinstalling the MQTT integration re-discovered entities but required dashboard rebuilds.
stance_target: fleet documentation should pin one broker-auth pattern; auth-mode changes force integration reinstall with dashboard churn
quoted_support: The first time setting it up I followed the (supposedly wrong?) docs and created a 'homeassistant' login for MQTT ... The entities were re-discovered and reconnected to the previous data, but I had to remake the dashboard, which is quite annoying given the number of sensors.
